content: Auranofin is a medication prescribed to treat rheumatoid arthritis. It is used in combination with rest and non-drug therapies to alleviate symptoms such as painful, tender, or swollen joints and morning stiffness. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other conditions, so consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Auranofin is available in capsule form and is taken orally, usually once or twice daily. It is essential to take this medication on a regular schedule as directed by your doctor to achieve its full therapeutic effect. The benefits of auranofin may not be noticeable for 3 to 4 months, and in some individuals, it may take up to 6 months. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take auranofin exactly as prescribed, and do not take more or less than the recommended dose or take it more frequently than directed. Auranofin is sometimes used to treat psoriatic arthritis. If you are considering this medication for your condition, discuss the potential risks with your doctor. Before starting auranofin, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to auranofin or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and non-prescription medications you are taking, especially arthritis medications, phenytoin (Dilantin), and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of heart, kidney, or liver disease; diabetes; bleeding disorders; inflammatory bowel disease; colitis; rash; eczema; systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE); or bone marrow depression. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking auranofin, contact your doctor immediately. Avoid attempting to conceive while on auranofin and for at least 6 months after discontinuing the medication, as it remains in the body for an extended period. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking auranofin. Avoid consuming alcohol while on this medication. Minimize unnecessary or prolonged exposure to sunlight, and use protective clothing and sunscreen, as auranofin may increase your skin's sensitivity to sunlight. Auranofin may cause stomach upset. To reduce this effect, take the medication after meals or with a light snack. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. Space out the remaining doses for the day evenly. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Auranofin may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following minor side effects, especially if they persist or worsen: metallic taste, loose stools or diarrhea, stomach pain, upset stomach, vomiting, gas, or hair loss. If you experience any severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately. These include bloody or tarry stools, itching, skin rash, sore throat, mouth sores, fever, chills, unusual bruising or bleeding, blood in the urine, or fatigue. Serious side effects should also be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store auranofin in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as regular tests will be required to monitor your response to auranofin. If you undergo a tuberculin (TB) skin test, inform the healthcare provider that you are taking auranofin. Do not share your medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
